entries.title: U.S. inventor ages, gender and death dates matched to patents
entries.description: Author-built database matching U.S.-resident patent inventors to estimated birth years, inferred gender and some death dates collected from public web directories, linked to patents by inventor ID.
details: Personal data warning: the files contain inventor names, city and state of residence, estimated birth years and, for some inventors, death dates, collected from people-search websites. Use only for legitimate research, follow your institution's data-ethics rules, and do not use it to identify or contact individuals.

Quality caveats from the authors: ages come from heuristics and a quality score; death dates are described as less reliable. The checked age file has birth years from 1800 to 2013, so apply plausibility filters.

Twenty-three public files, 3 MB to 1.9 GB. The key files are the inventor age and gender table (2,408,326 rows; 1,858,516 unique inventors), a patent-to-inventor crosswalk (8,080,135 rows, grant years 1976 to 2018) and a death-date table. Other files were listed but not read.
Gender is inferred from first name and birth year by an algorithm; 571,074 rows are marked unknown.
The Dataverse record is marked CC0 1.0. Source websites for the scraped information may have their own terms.
A companion data paper (Kaltenberg, Jaffe and Lachman, “The Age of Invention”, NBER working paper 28768) documents the database.

entries.description: Author-released data behind a text-based measure of how differentiated a startup's founding strategy is. details: 102 files, about 11 GB, CC0. Only the 2003 text table was downloaded; later years were listed, not read.
